collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a large, heavy adult and another villager; in the story (name1) is a big, heavyset person)

collection.description: On tug-of-war day both teams want the big, strong villager as their anchor: bargain for them, or let them choose.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is big: broad, heavy and very strong. It's tug-of-war day, and both teams are arguing over who gets (subject) as their anchor at the back of the rope. (subject) is enjoying this very much, and is taking (subject.his/her) time deciding. (friend), captain of one team, is getting desperate.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (friend) offers the last piece of honey cake, a turn in the best hammock, and to do (subject)'s washing for a week. (subject) accepts all three. At the back of the rope, (subject) digs in (subject.his/her) heels and simply doesn't move. The other team pulls until their faces go purple. (friend)'s team wins. (subject) collects the honey cake with great dignity.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) chooses the other team, because they asked more politely. (friend)'s team loses, three times in a row, mostly by being dragged slowly across the grass while (subject) leans back and smiles. Afterward (friend) comes over, out of breath. "Next year," (friend.he/she) says, "I'm asking politely." (subject) laughs. "Next year I might be on your side."
